title: Mutual information under almost-everywhere substitution
statement: Let $(\Omega, \mu)$ be a measured space and let $S$ and $T$ be countable measurable spaces. Suppose $X, X' \colon \Omega \to S$ and $Y, Y' \colon \Omega \to T$ are maps with $X$ and $Y$ measurable, and that $X = X'$ and $Y = Y'$ hold $\mu$-almost everywhere. Then the mutual information is unchanged, $I[X : Y \,;\, \mu] = I[X' : Y' \,;\, \mu]$.
replaced:
If $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$ and $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$, then
$I[X : Y;\mu] = I[X' : Y';\mu]$.
